decisions.reason: A complete same-message MODIFY already records that the second V is locked and must be carried forward unchanged unless the client explicitly requests a change.
The client explicitly extends the locked-asset carry-forward policy to the Hero V, and no same-message MODIFY records that revision policy.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Kenji,

This round feels like a couple of steps backward because both the Hero V and the second V changed again.

Unless I explicitly request a change, neither V nor the É accent should be redrawn, refined, or reinterpreted. From this point forward, treat the Hero V, second V, and É accent as locked assets. Carry all three forward unchanged in every iteration, with every exploration taking place around those fixed elements.

My earlier feedback also appears to have been interpreted too literally. I am not asking the other letters to copy the Hero V’s left arm. They should instead feel as though the same hand designed them: their proportions, construction, and geometric language should relate naturally to the Hero V while the letters remain original. At present, the two parts still read as different design languages.

The 2nd milestone has been released. I’m looking forward to the next round.

value_updates.revision_policy: Treat the approved Hero V as a locked asset and carry it forward unchanged unless the client explicitly requests a change.

decisions.reason: Locking the three approved assets does not change the existing rule that they share one unified terminal gesture.
The asset-lock decision does not change the wordmark's established rhythm, kerning, hierarchy, or case treatment; duplicating the individual asset policies here would create an umbrella copy.

A complete same-message MODIFY already captures the changed relationship between the surrounding letterforms and the Hero V, while the lock on the three V-system assets does not otherwise alter this requirement.
The decision concerns preservation of approved geometry and does not change the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
Locking the Hero V, second V, and É accent does not alter the requirement for a wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
The asset revision policy does not change the established brand-expression goals or positioning constraints.
The decision to preserve three wordmark assets does not change the final production-ready artwork deliverable.
